description: Dev-set baseline on live data (10-DECISION decision 8): the evaluation oracle (evals/oracle, independent of ontology/operating) generates the day's dev items (F1-F4, closed transactions, run id live-<UTC date>) from GET-only Portal API, BC and Graph reads; a GET-only Portal mirror sync of the relations the curated schema binds for the items' root types and every type up to 2 declared links away, and the product's own GET-only BC capture, are projected into {tmp}; captured BC citations are re-read from that capture for the scorer. A Portal outage blocks parts, not the run (portal-indep pattern): items whose labels read the Portal are blocked_upstream (counted in eval.answer, never wrong) and the rest measure on the BC and document captures (eval.pass_rule portal_outage, eval.measured). Dev items related to a frozen held-out set (shared document, root or identifier; evals/partition.py) move out (eval.partition.moved_to_heldout) and the run leaves its digest manifest in the host state directory for the held-out check; every item then runs through the L10 runner (evals.runner.record) on a throwaway case host plus the generic tools plx.find/object/around/timeline, answered by the deterministic investigation path (evals/baseline.py; no model, no LLM call) and scored by the claim gate (evals/score.py). Questions the deterministic path has no plan for count as needs_agent, never as passes. Before each item the runner writes a run pin (docs/decisions/2026-10-02-oracle-pinning.md): per relation the expected citations name, the first completed mirror capture at or after the item's time; the scorer reads the pinned generation from it, and an expected cited field whose pinned mirror version differs from the oracle's read (field digest) makes the item pin_drift, counted and excluded from every rate. A run the scorer finds a read gap (it fails only on bc:// citations the harness could not re-read) is blocked, counted (eval.blocked) and in no rate either; eval.blocked_share is the blocked items over every item, and above evals.score.DRIFT_TRIPWIRE_SHARE (10%) the run fails (exit 3, eval.fail_reasons blocked_share) so a capture lag never silently shrinks the measured set. Publishes rates (x/y), outcome and failure-reason codes, counts and 16-hex hashes only; never an identifier, key, citation or row value; items and transcripts stay in memory/{tmp}.
notes: live-unverified until a passing live-check result; the keyless counterpart is the isolated-fixture baseline (python3 -m scripts.eval_dev_baseline fixture; evals/baseline/dev-fixture.json). Daily cadence: one oracle generation, a schema-derived mirror sync and a projection exceed the hourly budget; the whole run shares one 1800 s budget (the mirror sync keeps 600 s back for projection and items; timeout 1900 s), so the daily session stays about 2 h with mirror.full_coverage (3600 s) and mirror.relation_counts (1800 s) and a cut run reports eval.complete=false with eval.incomplete reasons (run_budget_exhausted, mirror_incomplete) and fails; a relation no family plan reads left unfinished is noted as eval.incomplete mirror_unplanned_unfinished (named in eval.mirror.unfinished) and leaves eval.complete true. The runner lifts the recorded eval block into results/latest.json eval['eval.dev_baseline']; python3 -m scripts.eval_status results/latest.json prints the line saved into state.status.eval. Exit 0 needs a complete run over >= 20 items on a non-empty projection, and the check passes only at B1's bar on eval.answer: accuracy_rate (correct/answered) >= 0.8, coverage_rate (answered over the items that ran; an abstention, justified or not, is not covered) >= 0.8 and confident_unsupported_rate (claim-gate-refused wrong answers stated without abstaining, over answered) <= 0.02, all three from evals.score.answer_rates (docs/decisions/2026-10-19-b1-one-answer-rate.md); a null rate (nothing answered) fails. Known honest limits: the scorer now scores calculated answers (sum/count/equal recomputed from cited values) and mail/SharePoint/BC capture citations, but F1/F2/F4 questions still need a planning model and count needs_agent (unscored_other in eval.answer) under the deterministic path. During a Portal outage the check is blocked in part (expect_blocked: at least one item measured on the BC/document captures, and those items held to the same B1 rates, else fail), never a pass; an outage that left nothing to measure says outage_unmeasured portal_outage and is blocked whole (blocked_when). The SharePoint folder paths are the same first guess as eval.oracle_dev. Session state: its requires are its session producers mirror.full_coverage ({session_state}/mirror.sqlite, Portal service audience) and ontology.session_projection, which never block it; it tops up the mirror when that producer filled it in the session (session_state.shared_store, producer_verdict, producer_run), else captures cold into it. It no longer shares bc.capture_full's {session_state}/bc-capture.sqlite: with the session projection it reads that projection's BC capture, and only its cold path captures BC itself (into {tmp}), so the daily rotation's producer chain for it (mirror.full_coverage, then ontology.session_projection) leaves out a BC capture it would not read. It copies the mirror once after its sync and its items link that copy (no copy per item); it projects only its own relations and BC entity sets, so a shared store that holds more changes neither the product nor its build time. Session projection (the answer to docs/decisions/2026-10-10-dev-baseline-projection-budget.md: option 3): it also requires ontology.session_projection, its session producer of {session_state}/projection (Portal and BC, service reader), which never blocks it. When this session committed that generation the run captures no BC and does not sync the whole mirror: it copies the producer's mirror snapshot once, tops up (GET-only, phase pin_sync, recorded as eval.mirror.pin_sync relations/complete/error_code) only the cited relations that hold no completed capture at or after the latest item's as_known_at.time (the producer may have captured before the oracle ran, which left F3/F4 pins at no_capture_at_or_after_time), then opens the generation read-only when every unit key matches (product.session_projection reused) and reads the producer's BC capture for the scorer, so the whole reserve goes to the items; else it tops up, captures and projects as before (phases mirror_sync, bc_capture, projection). Daily fit: as a reader that never runs cold (session_required, session_reads) its need in the daily command is its producers' last durations plus min(timeout, 1.5 x its last shared run), and its run is self-bounded (1800 s budget, then the watchdog 60 s later records and exits), so the 1900 s timeout is that bound plus 40 s; at the old 2400 s the 2026-10-19T09:37Z daily needed 1,539 + 3,174 + 2,400 = 7,113 s against 7,000 s and settled it session_over_budget, at 1900 s it needs 6,613 s. A daily whose producers last took more than 5,100 s together still settles it (the 5,620 s pair of 2026-10-19T17:23Z): the producers' build is the lever there (docs/decisions/2026-10-19-projection-shared-cost.md). Per-item record (102342432f14 items 2 and 4): item_rows holds one family-number:root:outcome:reason code per item (ids and reason codes only, no values; ':' keeps the scrubber off it) the oracle drew (root resolution, outcome and first reason of a measured item; not_measured with the phase a budget cut stopped; blocked_upstream for an item a Portal outage blocked), recorded last so it never crowds out the eval block; a cut before the items (mirror sync, copy, projection) still records items_total from the oracle.
